doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Born in South Dakota; father in the Air Force and Negro League
summary: His father, stationed in the Air Force and pitching in the Negro League, is in the Baseball Hall of Fame; Stewart was born in Sioux Falls and taken to New York.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And early on it looked like you moved around as a child? I just was reading a little bio about you and you were born in South Dakota but you didn’t stay there?
No I didn’t stay there. My father just happened to be stationed in the Air Force. At the time my father was kind of in the Air Force as well as playing in the Negro League, the baseball league.

He was in it through the forties, all through the forties he was in his late teens, early twenties, he played ball all through. He was an athlete and played ball all through college and played in the Negro League through the forties as well as was in the Air Force in the latter part of the forties. And my mother went out to visit him, he was in the Air Force, and they went out to visit him in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, and she was pregnant and I was born there. And so when she came out of the hospital she left and took me with her back to New York.
So you lived there for maybe a day and a half.
Yeah, maybe both weeks or something.
You know they just honored the Negro ball league in Cooperstown.

Right, just recently. In fact this is the second, it may have been more than the second but it was the second that I’ve heard of, coming of it. In 1991 was the first time they honored any remaining living members of the Negro League and he was inducted in the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1991 right here in Cooperstown, near here, right?
My father is in the Baseball Hall of Fame.
Isn’t that far out? And he was also, he had two or three interviews during the Ken Burns baseball ten episode series. It’s interesting, he’s in that one and I’m in the one on jazz.
That’s great, I’m going to look for you. Which episode is it, do you recall off hand?
I don’t remember off hand, like somewhere around three and four, but Reilly A. Stewart. Same initials as mine just different name.
